source_text: Huic sententiae contradicunt, qui arbitrantur istam communionem, quam siue deitatem siue dilectionem caritatemue appellamus, non. esse substantiam; quaerunt autem secundum substantiam sibi exponi spiritum sanctum, nec intellegunt non aliter potuisse dici: deus dilectio est, nisi substantia esset dilectio. ducuntur quippe consuetudine rerum corporalium, quoniam, si duo sibi corpora copulentur, ita ut iuxta inuicem conlocentur, ipsa copulatio non est corpus, quandoquidem separatis illis corporibus, quae copulata fuerant, nulla inuenitur; nec tamen quasi discessisse et migrasse intellegitur, sicut illa corpora. sed hi tales cor mundum faciant, quantum possunt, ut uidere ualeant in dei substantia non esse aliquid tale, quasi aliud ibi sit substantia, aliud quod accidat substantiae, et non sit substantia; sed quidquid ibi intellegi potest, substantia est. uerum haec dici possunt facile et credi; uideri autem nisi corde puro quomodo se habeant, omnino non possunt. quapropter siue ista uera sit sententia, siue aliud aliquid sit, fides inconcussa tenenda est, ut deum dicamus patrem, deum filium, deum spiritum sanctum, neque tres deos, sed istam trinitatem unum deum, neque diuersas naturas, sed eiusdem substantiae, neque ut pater aliquando sit filius, aliquando spiritus sanctus, sed pater semper pater et filius semper filius et spiritus sanctus semper spiritus sanctus. nec temere de inuisibilibus aliquid adfirmemus tamquam scientes, sed tamquam credentes, quoniam uideri nisi mundato corde non possunt. et si quis ea uidet in hac uita ex parte, ut dictum est, atque in aenigmate, non potest efficere, ut et ille uideat, cui loquitur, si cordis sordibus inpeditur. beati autem mundi corde, quoniam ipsi deum uidebunt. haec fides est de deo conditore et renouatore nostro.
thought_title: The Holy Spirit as the substance of love
orientation: Augustine is answering those who deny that the communion of Father and Son, called deity or love, is a substance, and he is defending the Holy Spirit's place in the one divine substance.
pass_a_gloss: To this opinion [they] contradict, who think that communion, which whether deity or love [or] charity [we] call, not to be substance; [they] seek moreover according to substance to themselves to be explained [the] holy spirit, nor [do they] understand not otherwise [it] could have been said: God love is, unless substance were love. [They] are led indeed by custom of bodily things, since, if two to themselves bodies [are] joined, so that next to each other [they] are placed, [the] joining itself is not body, since when [those] bodies [are] separated, which joined had been, none is found; nor yet as if [it] had departed and migrated [is it] understood, like those bodies. But these such [people] [their] heart pure [let them] make, as much as [they] can, so that to see [they] may be able in God's substance not to be something such, as if other there be substance, other what happens to substance, and not be substance; but whatever there [can] be understood, substance is. Truly these [things] [can] be said easily and believed; to be seen however unless [with] heart pure how [they] have themselves, entirely not [they] can. Wherefore whether this true be opinion, or other something be, faith unshaken [is] to be held, so that God [we] say [the] father, God [the] son, God [the] holy spirit, nor three gods, but that trinity one God, nor different natures, but of [the] same substance, nor that [the] father sometimes be [the] son, sometimes [the] holy spirit, but [the] father always [the] father and [the] son always [the] son and [the] holy spirit always [the] holy spirit. Nor rashly about invisible [things] anything [let us] affirm as if knowing, but as if believing, since to be seen unless [with] cleansed heart not [they] can. And if anyone sees them in this life in part, as [has been] said, and in [a] riddle, not [he] can bring [it] about, that also he sees, to whom [he] speaks, if by filth of heart [he] is hindered. Blessed moreover [are the] pure in heart, since they God will see. This faith is about God [the] creator and renewer our.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'charity' for dilectio, but here caritas is a separate word paired with dilectio; rendering caritas as 'charity' preserves the distinction between the two Latin terms.
This is the standard English rendering of the biblical phrase, and the glossary requires 'love' for dilectio.
The glossary requires 'substance' for substantia as the underlying reality or essence of God.
This keeps the concrete image of dirt or filth blocking spiritual sight, matching Augustine's contrast with a pure heart.
This echoes the traditional English rendering of 1 Corinthians 13:12, which Augustine is quoting.
This keeps the active agent sense of the Latin noun, describing God as the one who renews us.

bible_refs.note: beati autem mundi corde, quoniam ipsi deum uidebunt

pass_b_english: Some people contradict this view. They think that this communion—whether we call it deity or love or charity—is not a substance. They ask for the Holy Spirit to be explained to them according to substance, and they do not understand that it could not have been said, “God is love” (1 John 4:8), unless love were a substance. They are led astray by their familiarity with bodily things. If two bodies are joined together so that they are placed next to each other, the joining itself is not a body, since when those bodies that had been joined are separated, no joining is found. Yet it is not understood to have departed and moved away, as those bodies have. But let such people make their hearts as pure as they can, so that they may be able to see that in God’s substance there is nothing like this—as if substance were one thing there, and something else that happens to substance and is not substance. Whatever can be understood there is substance. These things can easily be said and believed, but how they actually are cannot be seen at all except by a pure heart. Therefore, whether this view is true or whether it is something else, the faith must be held unshaken: that we call God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit—not three gods, but this Trinity one God; not different natures, but of the same substance; not that the Father is sometimes the Son and sometimes the Holy Spirit, but the Father is always Father, the Son always Son, and the Holy Spirit always Holy Spirit. Let us not rashly affirm anything about invisible things as if we knew it, but as if we believed it, since they cannot be seen except by a purified heart. And if anyone sees them in this life in part, as it has been said, and in a riddle (1 Corinthians 13:12), he cannot make the person he is speaking to see them too, if that person is hindered by the filth of his heart. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God (Matthew 5:8). This is the faith about God our creator and renewer.

last_rejected.quote: not that the Father is sometimes the Son and sometimes the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: neque ut pater aliquando sit filius, aliquando spiritus sanctus
last_rejected.why: English adds 'is' twice, making it sound like modalism (one person changing roles); Latin says 'ut pater aliquando sit filius' = 'that the Father should ever be the Son', i.e., the persons do not swap identities.
last_rejected.fix: not that the Father should ever be the Son or ever be the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: 'Sometimes' captures 'aliquando'; 'is' is standard copula for 'sit'. No meaning change; modalism not implied.

last_rejected.quote: as if substance were one thing there, and something else that happens to substance and is not substance
last_rejected.source_quote: quasi aliud ibi sit substantia, aliud quod accidat substantiae, et non sit substantia
last_rejected.why: English 'happens to substance' weakens the technical term 'accidat' (accident); Augustine denies accidents in God, but 'happens to' obscures the philosophical claim.
last_rejected.fix: as if substance were one thing there, and something else that accrues to substance and is not substance
last_rejected.ruling: 'Happens to substance' is a valid rendering of 'accidat substantiae' within normal range; no meaning lost.
